title: Etaleness descends through a surjective etale source cover
statement: Let $T,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $h:X\to T$ and $p:Y\to X$ be morphisms. If $p$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $h\circ p$ is etale, then $h$ is etale. No separation, finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $T$, $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 036W, lemma-etale-etale-local-source, applied to the singleton etale covering p.

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] applied to $h\circ p$, this composite is smooth. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] with $X\prime=Y$, source map $q=p$ and structural map $f=h$. Its flatness, surjectivity and local-finite-presentation hypotheses on $q$ are precisely those just checked and the given surjectivity; its smooth-composite hypothesis is the preceding assertion. Hence $h$ is smooth. In particular $h$ is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. This application does not require $p$ to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 05B5, lemma-smooth-permanence, smooth case; this supplies the smoothness step of morphisms.tex Tag 02K6 (lemma-etale-permanence-two), cited by Tag 02KM in the proof of Tag 036W.

proof.text: Both $p$ and $h$ are locally of finite type. Here is the elementary implication from the local finite presentation already obtained. For either morphism $f$ and any affine target open $V$, the affine-basis assertion [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] covers $f^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], each corresponding algebra has the form $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$, where $R=\mathcal O(V)$. The images of the finitely many $t_i$ generate this algebra over $R$. This is exactly the affine-cover condition for local finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No finiteness of the open cover is needed.

source.place: Tag 01TW, lemma-finite-presentation-finite-type; the elementary argument expands the omitted proof using Tag 01TQ and schemes.tex Tag 01IT.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. By [def-weil-surjective-morphism], choose $y\in Y$ with $p(y)=x$, and put $t=h(x)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] to the two given etale morphisms $p$ and $h\circ p$. For their scheme-theoretic fibres it gives $\dim_y(Y_x)=0$ and $\dim_y(Y_t)=0$, respectively. Since $p$ is flat at $y$ and $p,h$ are locally of finite type by Steps 1--2, [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point], with $a=p$ and $f=h$, gives $$0=\dim_y(Y_t)=\dim_y(Y_x)+\dim_x(X_t)=0+\dim_x(X_t).$$ Thus $\dim_x(X_t)=0$. These are dimensions at a point of the fibres, not merely dimensions of their local rings. Each fibre considered contains the indicated point, even if other fibres are empty.

source.place: Tag 02K6, lemma-etale-permanence-two, proof: zero relative dimensions and Tag 02JS (lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive), flat equality case; Tag 02GL and the remark after Definition 02GI identify the two zero dimensions.

proof.text: For each $x\in X$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-near-point-smooth-zero-fibre-dimension] to $h$, using global smoothness from Step 1 and $\dim_x(X_{h(x)})=0$ from Step 3. It provides an open neighbourhood $U_x\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $h$ is etale. The $U_x$ cover $X$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] shows that $h$ is etale. If $X$ is empty, its empty open covering satisfies the same locality statement, so this argument also includes the empty case. Surjectivity of $p$ forces $X$ to be empty whenever $Y$ is empty. All invoked results are local statements over arbitrary schemes; none adds separation, global finite type or Noetherian assumptions.

source.place: Tag 02K6, lemma-etale-permanence-two, conclusion; smooth relative dimension zero is etale, remark after Definition 02GI; Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize, locality on the source.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02K6 (lemma-etale-permanence-two), smoothness and additive fibre-dimension proof, as used through descent.tex Tag 02KM in Tag 036W. The otherwise missing local finite presentation is obtained together with smoothness from the smooth case of descent.tex Tag 05B5; Tag 01TW is expanded elementarily.
